audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer states twice that Zac has no percent-health damage: "no true damage or percent-HP on Zac means stacked Q, ult and lifesteal beat his fat HP bar" and "Zac has no true damage and no percent-HP shred".
audit.why: Unstable Matter is percent-max-health damage by definition — "Zac explodes outward towards nearby enemies, dealing a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage" — on a flat 5 second cooldown, and Cell Division carries the percentHealth flag as well. This is the exact stat the rest of the guide tells Nasus to stack: Doran's Shield start, Fury of the Sands' bonus Health, a tank item. The text reassures the reader that the one thing punishing their build does not exist.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter deals a percentage of your maximum health as magic damage every 5 seconds, so raw HP feeds it. Armour and anti-heal are the answer.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — W description, kitFlags.percentHealth = ["P","W"]

audit.whatIsWrong: Cell Division's revive is absent from the content layer entirely, and the full layer only gestures at it with "Step on his blobs" and "Let him eat blobs" without ever explaining what the blobs do or naming the cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Upon taking fatal damage, Zac splits into 4 bloblets that attempt to recombine. If any bloblets remain, he will revive with an amount of Health depending on the Health of the surviving bloblets. This ability has a 5 minute cooldown." Two separate things are being called blobs — the chunks he sheds on every ability hit for sustain, and the four bloblets he leaves on death. The five-minute number is the single most decisive fight-or-don't-fight fact in the matchup: once the revive is spent, Zac is a normal champion for five minutes, and Nasus is a melee champion standing right on top of the bloblets who is unusually well placed to deny the recombine.
audit.corrected: Cell Division revives him from four bloblets on a 5-minute cooldown — stand on them after the kill, and if it is already spent he is simply killable.

audit.whatIsWrong: The sustain blobs are attributed to W — "Zac's W blob trades and passive blob sustain", "W blob trades and passive blob pickups", "Use E sling and W blob trades".
audit.why: The blobs come from Cell Division, the passive, and they are shed on hits from any ability, not from W specifically. W is Unstable Matter, the percent-health explosion. Splitting the credit correctly matters because it tells the reader that every single ability Zac lands generates a heal pickup — so denying blobs is a constant job, not something that only happens when he casts one particular spell.
audit.corrected: Every ability he lands sheds a Cell Division blob he can walk back over to heal. W is Unstable Matter, the percent-health explosion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing notes that Zac has no mana and pays current health for Q, W and E.
audit.why: Zac's resource is None and Stretching Strikes, Unstable Matter and Elastic Slingshot all cost a percentage of current health. He cannot be mana-starved, but he damages himself every time he uses his kit — which is precisely why denying the blob pickups works, and why sustained chip from a lingering Spirit Fire zone compounds against him faster than against a mana champion. This is the mechanical justification for the full layer's "deny blobs, anti-heal" win condition, which is currently asserted without a reason.
audit.corrected: Every cast costs him current health, so chip damage plus denied blobs bleeds him out — that is why the anti-heal plan works.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json — resource "None", Q/W/E costType "% of current Health"

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Elastic Slingshot as matchup-defining with no number, and no concrete timing appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9 — a 21 second window at rank 1, one of the longest non-ultimate cooldowns Nasus gets to play around, and it shrinks by more than half by rank 5. Unstable Matter at a flat 5s is the one that governs standing next to him. Cell Division's revive at 5 minutes is the longest and most important.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot 21s at rank 1. Unstable Matter flat 5s. Cell Division revive 5 minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, although the full layer's win condition is literally "deny blobs, anti-heal, out-scale".
audit.why: Cell Division carries the heal flag and is the sustain engine of the matchup. The two layers disagree on the plan: full says anti-heal is the win condition, content says lifesteal and stacked Q simply out-grind him. Only one of those survives contact with a Zac reabsorbing a blob from every ability he lands.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds plus physically walking over the shed blobs is what breaks his sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: full.diff is "EVEN" at 6/10 and the full phase chart gives Zac stages 1-4, for a lane Nasus wins 55.87%.
audit.why: The content chart is the honest one here — Zac 2, Skill 2, Nasus 3 — and matches a clearly Nasus-favoured result. The full layer reads as an even-to-losing lane. Not submitted as an edit for the same reason as elsewhere in this slice: the ±10% band cannot replace "Zac" with "Skill" or "Nasus" in a .side field, and I do not know the permitted diff values.
audit.corrected: full.phases[2..3].side and full.diff should follow the content chart and the 55.87% result.
sources: packet winRate 55.87 / 349 games; champ-data/content/nasus.js win[], champ-data/nasus.full.js phases[].side and diff

notes: The headline error is that the content layer twice tells the reader Zac has no percent-health damage, when Unstable Matter is percent-max-health magic damage on a flat 5-second cooldown. That is not a naming slip — it actively endorses the HP-stacking build the ability punishes, including Nasus's own Fury of the Sands bonus health. Second, Cell Division's revive never appears in the content layer at all, and the full layer references 'blobs' three times without ever distinguishing the sustain chunks shed on every ability hit from the four bloblets he leaves on death, or naming the 5-minute cooldown that decides whether a kill will actually stick. Also worth flagging that the two layers disagree on the win condition: full says 'deny blobs, anti-heal, out-scale' while content says lifesteal and stacked Q out-grind him without ever mentioning Grievous Wounds. I did not use Elastic Slingshot's grounding flag — Nasus has no dash, so per the relevance rule there was nothing to say.
